headline: Livemint reports that C.C. Wei, chief executive of TSMC, said demand for its advanced chips is extremely robust and that it wants every piece of business it can get, while CNBC reports a fierce battle among Nvidia, Apple and Broadcom for its factory space.
score_reason: Kept at 6: the record quarter and the demand statements are confirmed, while the contest for space among Nvidia, Apple and Broadcom rests on CNBC alone.
importance_line: TSMC makes chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and Broadcom, so how it shares out its scarce factory space shapes who gets AI and phone chips first, though how it is dividing that space among them has not been made public.
source: Livemint, citing TSMC's earnings call; CNBC reports the capacity contest
summary: Livemint reports that C.C. Wei, chairman and chief executive of TSMC, the Taiwanese company that makes chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and Broadcom, said on its earnings call on 15 October that demand for advanced chips remains "extremely robust" and that "we want to capture every piece of business possible", after TSMC posted a record third-quarter net profit of NT$763.1 billion (about $23.6 billion), up 68.7% from a year earlier. Taiwan's Central News Agency adds that TSMC raised its 2026 sales growth forecast to 44% and kept its capital spending plan at $60 billion to $64 billion, though Wei said it is planning cautiously for 2027 because rising component prices and economic uncertainty are hurting price-sensitive markets.
notes: Read Livemint's and Focus Taiwan's reports of the 15 Oct TSMC call. CNBC's headline says Nvidia, Apple and Broadcom are in a 'fierce' battle for TSMC capacity; that detail was not found in the text read, so it is attributed to CNBC and not expanded.
